speakerposition: Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs; Minister of Mines; Minister of the Interior
subtopic: PAPERS TABLED RESPECTING DIVERSION OF WATER
speechtext:
I desire to
place upon the table a return asked for by the hon. member for St. Lawrence-St. George, the subject being the report of the three' Canadian members of the International Waterways Commission dated on or about April 5, 1906, recommending the negotiation of a treaty with the United States. I should like, with the indulgence of the house, to make a short statement in regard to these important documents.
Incorporated with the material which is being tabled to-day regarding the Chicago diversion is a series of exchanges between the Canadian and United States governments, which has taken place subsequent to the exchanges tabled on February 24, 1926. In view of the complexity of the Chicago diversion matter and of the lengthy nature of this recent correspondence an explanatory statement with respect to it is desirable.
The tabling of this further correspondence will demonstrate the careful manner in which the interests of Canada have been continuously guarded by the Canadian government as the Chicago situation has developed from month to month.
On February 24, 1926, there was tabled in the House of Commons an interchange of correspondence between the Canadian government and that of the United States with respect to the matter of the withdrawal of water from the great lakes system by the Chicago sanitary district. In my statement to the house at that time, covering the correspondence then tabled, I mentioned the fact that on January 5. 1926, the Canadian government,
having secured an official interpretation by the United States government of the permit which the United States Secretary of War had issued on March 3, 1925, in favour of the Chicago sanitary district, had set forth its position in a comprehensive manner in a further despatch, dated February 4, 1926, which included a protest against then pending proposals for the construction of a nine-foot navigable channel in the Illinois and Mississippi rivers, based upon the diversion of
10,000	cubic feet per second from the great lakes through the sanitary district canal, and that this despatch had been withheld from publication, in accordance with an understanding with the government of the United States.
In the interval which elapsed pending the receipt of the reply of the United States government to this note, and because of the increasing concern arising from the progress of the Mississippi waterway measure before congress, the government of Canada sent a further communication to the government of the United States on April 30, 1926, drawing the attention of that government to the international aspect of the matter and protesting vigorously against the action contemplated by the measure.
At about the same date the Dominion government was in receipt of a communication from the government of the province of Ontario, transmitting a copy of a resolution of the legislative assembly of that province also protesting against the enactment by the United States congress of any legislation authorizing the abstraction of water from the great lakes system at Chicago. This protest was also formerly transmitted to the United States government on April 23, 1926,
A response to the Canadian government s representations was received on July 26, 1926, which among other things, advised that the bill which had been before congress and which had had in view the authorization of a diversion of 10,000 cubic feet per second from great lakes system to the Illinois and Mississippi rivers, had not been enacted into law during the session of congress then recently closed, and advised further, however, that the bill would be taken up for consideration shortly after the next session of congress which convened in December.
To follow this point further I might state that the Mississippi waterway measure was considered by the reassembled congress in December and was passed with a reference to the 10,000 cubic feet per second diversion deleted, and with an amendment added to the effect "that nothing in this act shall be con-
Chicago Drain-age Canal

strued as authorizing any diversion of water from lake Michigan." In view of the consistent protests which the government of Canada had registered in opposition to the principles embodied in the Mississippi waterway measure as first introduced, the amendment to the bill should give ground for a considerable measure of satisfaction on the part of the people of Canada. This amendment removed the objections of the lake bordering states which had been vigorously fighting the proposal in congress, and would appear to have very largely met the objectionable features inherent in the original bill.
Furthermore, in response to a specific inquiry made in the Canadian government's despatch of January 5th, 1926, as to what progress had been attained by the Chicago sanitary district and by the municipality of Chicago in the provision of the curtailment measures called for by the permit of the United States Secretary of War, dated March 3, 1925-under which authority the diversion is now being made-the United States government in its despatch of July 26th, informed the Canadian government:
(a)	That preliminary investigations had been made with regard to the installation of controlling works at the intake to the sanitary canal, and that it was expected that detail plans would be prepared during the ensuing year, and that no difficulty in the completion of these works prior to the expiration of the permit was anticipated.
(b)	That the progress made by the city of Chicago in carrying out the installation of sewage treatment works was satisfactory.
(c)	That it was expected that the installation of water meters would, in the near future, result in a reduction in the consumption of water used for domestic purposes.
From the statements made by the United States government as to the progress made by the Chicago sanitary .district in meeting the conditions of the Secretary of War's permit we would be warranted in assuming that the United States government was satisfied that the progressive reduction which it anticipated in its note of November 24, 1925, would be realized. This note anticipatel a reduction by December 31, 1929, to 8.000 cubic feet per second and probably 6,700 cubic feet per second, and stated further that the sewage treatment program of the sanitary district had been arranged so as to make it possible to effect a reduction to a gross flow of 4,167 cubic feet per second by the year 1935 or before.
The subsequent exchange of correspondence tabled to-day has to do mainly with the securing of the assent of the United States governfMr. C. A. Stewart.]
ment to the publication of the despatches to which I have just referred. This was formally requested in a communication from the Canadian government dated November 16, 1926.
In a response dated December 7, 1926, the United States government expressed the view that the report of the Joint Board of Engineers on the St. Lawrence waterway project had greatly altered the understanding of the situation with respect to diversions from great lakes watersheds, and that it would, therefore, be unjustifiable to publish the correspondence which was based upon, at least, a partial misapprehension of the facts. The note pointed out that there had been a general impression in many parts of Canada and United States that the fall of some thirty inches in lake levels was very largely due to the diversion at Chicago, whereas, the joint board's report showed that only a small part of the fall in lake levels had been due to that diversion. The note further suggested that the two governments enter upon a discussion of the practical question of providing compensatory works as recommended by the Joint Board of Engineers.
In the response of the Canadian government, dated September 1, 1927, the Canadian government pointed out that it had not been under any misapprehension as to the extent which the abstraction of water through the Chicago sanitary canal had lowered the levels of the great lakes, and that it had been fully advised that this lowering had been in the neighbourhood of six inches, and pointed out that if any misapprehension existed in the United! States or in Canada as to the degree of lowering occasioned by the Chicago abstraction, the publication of these papers would go a long way towards relieving such misunderstanding.
The Canadian note furthermore pointed out that the installation of compensatory works for the restoration of lake levels would in no way recoup to the great lakes system, the power which is lost to that system by water abstracted therefrom through the sanitary canal, and that while recognizing the marked advantages which may be gained by the construction of suitable compensating works, Canada would not be prepared to enter upon a discussion of any plans for the construction of such works if this course involved an assumption that the present abstraction through the Chicago sanitary canal is to continue. A further suggestion that the correspondence be published was incorporated in the Canadian note.
In the United States government's response the suggestion as to the publication of the
correspondence was accepted incorporating,

St. John Harbour Commission
however, in the series to be published, a further despatch dated October 17, 1927, in which it inferred that the apportionment of water for power purposes at Niagara under which Canada receives 36,000 cubic feet per second, and the United States, 20,000 cubic feet per second, was in compensation for the abstraction of water by Chicago. It is hardly necessary to state that the Canadian government does not concur in this viewpoint and that aJll Canadian governments have consistently taken the stand, in all protests made to the United States government, since the initiation of the abstraction of the water, that no compensation has anywhere or at any time been made for the Chicago withdrawal.
The house is also aware of the suit which is now pending before the United States Supreme Court, under which the states of Wisconsin, Ohio, Pensylvania, and Minnesota, with the support also of the states of Michigan, and New York, are questioning the legality of the permits which have been issued by the United States Secretary of War to the Chicago sanitary district authorizing the withdrawal of water through the Chicago sanitary canal, and questioning further the right even of congress to authorize such withdrawal from the great lakes system.
This suit in the United States Supreme Court is, of course, a purely domestic matter with which the government of Canada has no direct contact and with respect to which it could not with any propriety taken any action or make any representations. I might add, however, that as the suit involves legal principles of the very highest importance to Canada, the progress is being followed with the utmost care, in order that the effect on Canadian interests of whatever decision is reached may be fully appreciated, and that any necessary action may be taken to protect those interests.
It will be evident from the foregoing that the Canadian government is maintaining the closest possible contact with every phase and feature having to do with the Chicago diversion. The government of Canada has consistently refused to recognize the diversion in the slightest measure and will continue to present the Canadian viewpoint with all possible firmness to the United States government against the entire principle of abstracting water from the great lakes to another watershed.

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES

speechtext:
Hon. P. J. A. CARDIN (Minister of Marine and Fisheries) moved that the house go into committee to consider the following resolution:
That it is expedient to authorize a loan to the harbour commissioners of Saint John in an amount not exceeding $5,000,000 to enable the corporation to construct such terminal facilities as are necessary properly to equip the port of Saint John, upon approval by the governor in council of detailed plans, specifications and estimates for such works, and the deposit of debentures of the corporation to cover said loan.

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext:
Perhaps the minister
would be good enough, in a clear and concise way, to tell us the circumstances under Which this resolution is being moved. This is a large sum of money and we should like to know just what is involved in it and what obligations the country accepts, in order that there may be no misunderstanding as apparently there was in another case. It seems to me we should get a statement of that kind from the minister in the case of this harbour commission which is coming to parliament for a grant for the first time since it came into existence.

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: The conditions in connection with the placing of the harbour of St. John under the harbour commissioners are embodied in the act under which the commission was created. The total consideration for the transfer of the harbour to the commissioners amounted to 12,135,118, apportioned as follows: existing bonded indebtedness of the city occasioned in the development of the harbour, to be taken over by the harbour commissioners, $1,467,164; balance to be paid to the city in harbour commissioners' bonds, $667,953.04. Of course this does not include the expenditure made through the Department of Public Works; it covers only the expenditure made by the city of St. John. As we all know, St. John harbour is a very old one, having been established in 1783.

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: Are those bonds to be a first charge, first mortgage bond?

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: Guaranteed?

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: There is no guarantee.

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: I mean the $600,000 bond to which the minister has referred, to be given to the city of St. John?

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: This will be the payment.

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: Cash payment?

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: Yes, that the government is supposed to make to the commission.

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext:
As I understand the
matter, the Dominion of Canada has bought the harbour?

St. John Harbour Commission

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: Assuming obligations for $1,500,000 and paying some $600,000 in bonds; is that correct?

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: Harbour commissioners' bonds?

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: To be paid to the city in harbour commissioners' bonds. The commissioners themselves are going to pay the city of St. John by bonds of the St. John harbour commission as created last year, the sum of $667,000.

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: What rate of interest?

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: Five per cent, the rate which is. charged to all the commissions.

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: It is the commissioners who are buying the harbour?

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: How was the price arrived at?

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: It was a valuation.

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: By whom?

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: By the engineers of the Department of Public Works.

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: No arbitration?

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: No.

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: Do I understand that the $600,000 worth of bonds of the harbour commission are to be given to the city of St. John in addition to the $5,000,000 worth of bonds that will be issued by the Dominion government for this loan?

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext:
Yes. The program which has been presented to us by the commissioners of St. John requests an amount of $10,000,000 for the work that they were disposed to undertake after careful examination by their engineers, but it has been agreed that $5,000,000 would satisfy them and would cover a program of three years' development. The statement which is given to me is that the initial development proposed with the loan now asked for would provide working space for four vessels loading general cargo and two vessels loading grain, and it includes the necessary dredging to provide basins and a channel of thirty feet at low water, to be increased to 35 feet should that later be found necessary. There will also be provided a new grain elevator; with a capacity of
2,400,000	bushels, with grain conveyor galleries connecting with two of the new berths. The

new shipping berths will be equipped with one storey freight sheds 575 feet by 90 feet. The work is to be undertaken with the idea of providing a complete unit of development ready for operation within the term of three years over which the loan is to be spread, as provided for in this bill.
As was stated this afternoon in the course of the discussion on another proposal, these developments in the port of St. John are recommended by the Duncan commission. This is what is said by the Duncan commission in regard to the matter:
We recommend that, in respect of each of these two harbours-
That is St. John and Halifax.
-the federal government should establish a statutory harbour commission, whose business it would be to see that the port facilities are developed on such a scale as will gradually- but by no means slowly-create channels through which trade can expand both winter and summer.
It is pursuant to these recommendations of the Duncan commission that we have incorporated the present harbour commission to take over the harbour, and following that recommendation we are accepting part of the program which has been suggested by the present harbour commission. I may say for the information of the committee that the gross earnings in 1927 amounted to $257,704.97 and the expenditures to $218,462.80.

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: Does that include the interest charges?

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: The interest on the city's own indebtedness.

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: In 1926-27, with the present elevator facilities, they handled 25,855,000 bushels.

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: Does that mean if the present rate of earnings is maintained, the interest on the bonds will be earned in part?

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: I do not think I can say that interest on the $5,000,000 for which they are asking will be met for some time. The commissioners do not expect to be in a position for some years to pay interest on this amount.

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: Is the $5,000,000 for the completion of one unit of development?

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext:
Is that really $5,000,000,
or does it mean $10,000,000?

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext:
The amount required for the whole development which they have in

view is 810,000,000, but they have represented to the department that with 85,000,000 they are capable of building a complete unit.

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext: The minister does not expect that there will be any interest chargeable during construction?

maintopic: ST. JOHN HARBOUR COMMISSION LOAN OF 85,000,000 FOR TERMINAL FACILITIES
speechtext:
No. The interest will be retained by the Minister of Finance.
Progress reported.

At eleven o'clock the house adjourned, without question put, pursuant to standing order.
Friday, April 20, 1928.
